Depth levels and the slabs they stand for

Source: vignettes/depth-levels.Rmd
depth-levels.Rmd

A SpatVoxel samples the water column at a set of depth levels, such as the World Ocean Atlas standard depths. A SpatEnvelope stores a continuous [depth_min, depth_max] interval per cell. Converting between the two with envelope_to_voxel(), or combining them with terra::mask(), intersect_3d(), intersects_3d() or volume(), needs a rule for which levels an interval occupies. This article sets out that rule.

The examples use a two-cell footprint, so every result can be printed in full.

library(ocean3d)

fp <- terra::rast(nrows = 1, ncols = 2, xmin = 0, xmax = 2, ymin = 0, ymax = 1)
terra::values(fp) <- c(1, 1)

A depth level stands for a slab, not a knife edge

A cell occupies a level when its envelope overlaps the slab that level stands for by more than a shared edge. This matters for thin intervals. An envelope of [10, 20] contains none of c(0, 100, 200), but it is clearly within the water the 0 m level represents:

thin <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 10, depth_max = 20)
terra::values(envelope_to_voxel(thin, depths = c(0, 100, 200)))
#>      presence_depth=0 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=200
#> [1,]                1                 NA                 NA
#> [2,]                1                 NA                 NA

Touching is not overlapping

By default the slab edges fall halfway between neighbouring levels, so with levels at 0, 50, 150 and 200 m one edge falls at 100 m. An envelope of [0, 100] ends exactly where the 150 m slab begins, so it occupies the 0 m and 50 m levels and not the 150 m one:

levels <- c(0, 50, 150, 200)
upper <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 0, depth_max = 100)
lower <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 100, depth_max = 200)

terra::values(envelope_to_voxel(upper, depths = levels))
#>      presence_depth=0 presence_depth=50 presence_depth=150 presence_depth=200
#> [1,]                1                 1                 NA                 NA
#> [2,]                1                 1                 NA                 NA

Two envelopes that meet at 100 m therefore do not intersect. intersects_3d() gives the same answer for the envelopes themselves and for their voxels, which land on disjoint levels:

terra::values(intersects_3d(upper, lower))
#>      intersects
#> [1,]      FALSE
#> [2,]      FALSE

terra::values(intersects_3d(
  envelope_to_voxel(upper, depths = levels),
  envelope_to_voxel(lower, depths = levels)
))
#>      intersects
#> [1,]      FALSE
#> [2,]      FALSE

Where the slab edges fall: bounds

Where the slab edges fall is a property of the dataset the levels came from, so bounds selects the convention:

  • "midpoint" (the default) puts the edges halfway between neighbouring levels. This matches World Ocean Atlas levels. It is close for model output such as Copernicus Marine, which stores values at the middle of each layer, but it leaves out the water above the shallowest level and below the deepest.
  • "top" runs each slab from its level down to the next, so each level is the top of its slab.

An interval of [60, 70] lands in a different level under each:

shallow <- as_envelope(fp, depth_min = 60, depth_max = 70)

terra::values(envelope_to_voxel(shallow, depths = c(0, 100, 200)))
#>      presence_depth=0 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=200
#> [1,]               NA                  1                 NA
#> [2,]               NA                  1                 NA
terra::values(envelope_to_voxel(shallow, depths = c(0, 100, 200),
                                bounds = "top"))
#>      presence_depth=0 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=200
#> [1,]                1                 NA                 NA
#> [2,]                1                 NA                 NA

The same bounds argument is accepted by terra::mask(), intersect_3d() and intersects_3d() wherever they place an envelope or SpatVector3D polygons on a voxel’s depth levels, by vector3d_to_voxel(), and by volume() to measure a voxel. Use the same value in intersect_3d() and in volume() when measuring its result. See ?envelope_to_voxel for the full rule, including how the shallowest and deepest levels are clamped.

A dataset’s own edges: depth_bounds

Both conventions work the edges out from the levels. When the dataset gives its own edges, for example a netCDF file’s depth bounds, a SpatVoxel can carry them: pass them to as_voxel() or envelope_to_voxel() as depth_bounds, a two-column table of top and bottom with one row per level. envelope_to_voxel() and the functions listed above then use these edges and ignore bounds, and depth_bounds() reads them back:

edges <- cbind(c(0, 65, 150), c(65, 150, 250))
v <- envelope_to_voxel(shallow, depths = c(0, 100, 200), depth_bounds = edges)
terra::values(v)
#>      presence_depth=0 presence_depth=100 presence_depth=200
#> [1,]                1                  1                 NA
#> [2,]                1                  1                 NA
depth_bounds(v)
#>   depth lower upper
#> 1     0     0    65
#> 2   100    65   150
#> 3   200   150   250

Here the 0 m level’s slab runs to 65 m, so [60, 70] occupies both the 0 m and the 100 m levels, where "midpoint" gave only the 100 m level.
